newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares consolidate in late IBIS dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares consolidate in late IBIS dealings.

text.p: German shares were lower in late dealings on Tuesday and at fresh session lows as traders said the market was searching for footing after the recent advance to new all-time record levels.
The IBIS DAX was down 48.69 points at 4,351.61 points, hurt by the weaker dollar and early losses on Wall Street. The DAX had ended bourse trade up 10.53 points at 4,381.69 points.
Traders expected the IBIS DAX to end post-bourse computer dealings in minus territory but noted that the upward trend was still intact and that the market was in a consolidative tone.
"The pressure from America became too much," said one Frankfurt dealer. "They are lower, so we are lower too."
Dealers said a lack of fresh impulses kept the market on the defensive, while some said the DAX index was merely out of breath after rising as much as 615 points in July.
"We need to take a break," said one dealer. "We are not going to head much lower but we needed some consolidation."
A flood of corporate earnings results, particularly in the banking sector, gave the market fresh fundamentals during morning dealings to digest.

Dresdner Bank AG ended the bourse up 2.35 marks at 85.20 marks after saying it planned to raise its base capital by 120 million marks by issuing new shares and was keen to expand activities in the United States.
The bank, the second-largest in Germany, also said earnings were up 23 percent in the first half of the year.
Commerzbank AG, considered the next target after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank said they will merge, ended up five pfennigs at 61.75 marks.
Carmaker BMW AG slumped 25 marks to 1,450 marks despite reporting a first-half group net profit of 435 million marks.
The profit figure was viewed as being slightly above market expectations for about 400 million marks.
Dealers said other carmakers were benefiting from the positive outlook for the sector, which has been bolstered by the weak mark making exports more competitve.
Daimler-Benz AG, maker of Mercedes vehicles, surged 3.55 marks to 156.45 marks as traders set a near-term target of 160 marks. Daimler will release six-month results on Thursday.
Degussa AG, the metal and chemicals group, was up 3.60 marks at 104.70 marks after reporting a 10 percent rise in nine-month group sales to 11.2 billion marks.
Degussa also said it expected a higher profit for the 1996/97 year.

Among other shares posting notable losses in early dealings were sportswear group Puma AG, which was down 2.10 marks at 52.80 marks on more volatile dealings amid fresh takeover talk for the Herzogenaurach-based group.
